content.key_idea: Splitting each Gaussian's rendering into an independent alpha stage and a dependent color stage lets an idle GPE pre-compute alpha for a busy GPE, balancing load across the GPE array.
content.reading_order: Panel (a) unbalanced timeline first, then panel (b) the rebalanced timeline, then panel (c) the hardware (scheduler, workload table, alpha buffer) that implements it.

summary: This figure explains AGS's fix for unbalanced GPE (Gaussian Processing Element) workloads during rendering. Panel (a) shows a timeline where GPE1 finishes after two Gaussians while GPE2 needs six, leaving GPE1 idle for 66% of the time, because Gaussian rendering splits into an independent alpha-computation stage and a data-dependent color-rendering stage. Panels (b) and (c) show the fix: a GPE scheduler consults a workload table to assign an idle GPE (GPE1) to pre-compute alpha values for a busy GPE's (GPE2's) remaining Gaussians, storing results in a tagged alpha buffer that the busy GPE later hits to skip redundant work. The figure is drawn as small Gantt-style per-GPE timelines next to a block diagram of the scheduler, workload table, alpha buffer and Gaussian feature buffer.
